Chapter 25
Diseases of the Musculoskeletal System  795
Medical Diagnosis and Clinical 
Manifestations
SLE is diagnosed based on the presence in the blood of a va-
riety of antibodies capable of damaging one’s own tissues (au-
toantibodies) and certain clinical features that are uncovered 
during a thorough physical exam and medical history. Th e
most common early symptoms of SLE are pain and arthritis in 
multiple joints (similar to that seen in RA), which can occur
in as many as 90% of patients.47 Also common are fatigue and 
muscle pain. Th e onset of SLE can be rapid or very slow
